logp.method_description: Information about the lipophilicity of the 64Cu-labelled cyclam propionic acid ligands was obtained by using water/1-octanol mixtures. The experiments were performed with 100 μM solutions of cyclam propionic acid ligands dissolved in 1-octanol. The aqueous phases consisted of 0.05 M HEPES/NaOH buffer (440 μL; pH 7.2, 7.4 or 7.6), [64Cu]CuCl2 solution (10 μL, 500 kBq), and a 100 μM Cu(NO3)2 solution (50 μL). The distribution experiments were performed at (25 ± 1) °C in microcentrifuge tubes (2 cm3) with mechanical shaking for 30 min. The phase ratio V(1-octanol)/V(aq) was 1:1 (0.5 mL each). Full complexation was checked by radio-HPLC, which provided no evidence of free copper(II) species in the aqueous phase. All samples were centrifuged, and the phases were then separated. The concentration of the copper complex in both phases was determined radiometrically by using γ radiation [64Cu, NaI(Tl) scintillation counter automatic γ counter 1480, Wizard 3″, Perkin–Elmer]. The results are the average values of three independent experiments.
